name: Retinal Ciliopathy

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding ciliary proteins associated with retinal degeneration
Clinical evidence of retinal dystrophy characterized by photoreceptor dysfunction and progressive vision loss
Abnormal electroretinogram (ERG) showing reduced or absent rod and/or cone responses
Retinal imaging (OCT, fundus autofluorescence) demonstrating photoreceptor layer thinning and retinal pigment epithelium changes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic variants in ciliary genes plus clinical evidence of retinal degeneration
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by electrophysiological and imaging findings; genetic testing is critical for confirmation.

searchTerms: gradual rod and cone photoreceptor loss
progressive night and day vision impairment
mild balance problems related to night blindness
balance issues linked to poor night vision

rare.symptomName: Associated systemic ciliopathy features (e.g., renal cystic disease)
searchTerms: kidney cysts and other systemic features
multiple organ involvement with cystic disease

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying mutations in ciliary genes (e.g., CEP290, RPGR, BBS genes)
imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing photoreceptor layer thinning
Fundus autofluorescence demonstrating retinal pigment epithelium abnormalities
Electroretinogram (ERG) with reduced or absent rod and cone responses
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding ciliary proteins implicated in retinal degeneration
other: Multisystem involvement in syndromic forms (e.g., Bardet-Biedl syndrome, Joubert syndrome)

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily retinal degeneration without systemic ciliopathy features
Genetic mutations not always involving ciliary genes
May share genetic overlap but typically presents in infancy
Retinal dystrophy with systemic features including obesity, polydactyly, renal anomalies
Syndromic ciliopathy with broader multisystem involvement

redFlags: Rapid progression of visual field loss
Early onset night blindness in childhood
Presence of systemic features suggestive of syndromic ciliopathy (e.g., renal cysts, polydactyly)
references: Waters AM, Beales PL. Ciliopathies: an expanding disease spectrum. Pediatr Nephrol. 2011;26(7):1039-1056.
Bujakowska KM, et al. Retinal ciliopathies: a review of clinical and molecular findings. Hum Genet. 2017;136(9):1039-1054.
